input: Subscribe to an online course for public speaking

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Public speaking covers many sub-skills (overcoming fear, structuring talks, presentation design, storytelling, etc.) — knowing which aspect to focus on changes which course is best.
Whether this is for the user themselves or someone else (e.g. a team member, a child) affects the level, tone, and type of course to look for.
The setting where they will apply the skill (corporate presentations, TEDx-style talks, classroom teaching, social situations) shapes which course content is most relevant.
Budget tolerance varies widely — free courses (YouTube, Coursera audit) vs. paid premium programs (e.g. MasterClass, Dale Carnegie) are very different options.
Some learners prefer self-paced video lessons; others want live coaching, peer feedback, or community practice — this directly determines which platform fits.
Knowing the target outcome (e.g. deliver a specific upcoming talk, pass a job interview, general long-term improvement) determines urgency and depth needed.
How much time per week they can dedicate affects whether a short intensive course or a long structured program is realistic.

gold.taskTitle: Subscribe to an online public speaking course
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to find and subscribe to an online course that will help them improve their public speaking skills.

questions.title: Which specific public speaking skill do you most want to improve?
questions.description: e.g. managing nerves, structuring a talk, vocal delivery, storytelling, handling Q&A — the focus area determines the best course content.

questions.title: Who is this course intended for?
questions.description: Is this for you personally, a colleague, a team, or someone else? This affects the appropriate level and framing of the course.

questions.title: In what setting will you apply your public speaking skills?
questions.description: e.g. corporate boardroom, conference stage, classroom, job interviews, social events — the context shapes which course focus is most useful.

questions.title: What is your budget for this course?
questions.description: Free, under $50, under $200, or open to premium programs like MasterClass or Dale Carnegie — budget narrows the platform shortlist dramatically.

questions.title: Do you prefer self-paced videos or live, interactive sessions?
questions.description: Some learners do best with flexible on-demand content; others need live coaching or peer practice groups to stay accountable and get feedback.

questions.title: Do you have a specific speaking event or deadline driving this?
questions.description: A looming presentation, pitch, or speech changes the urgency and depth of course needed versus general long-term skill building.

questions.title: How many hours per week can you dedicate to learning?
questions.description: This determines whether a short intensive crash course or a longer structured multi-week program is realistic and sustainable for you.
